--- page 8 ---
Table (Tableau 1: Calendrier saisonnier avec risque d'inondations): monthly calendar jan–déc showing Saison sèche (dry season) vs Saison de pluie (rainy season); "Haut risque d'inondations pluviales" marked X for juillet–septembre (rainfall flood risk); "Haut risque d'inondations fluviales" marked X for septembre(partial)–octobre through part of nov (riverine flood risk, roughly sep-nov).
Narrative text: flood impact history — 2019: >5,200 households affected, 13 deaths, 568 homes destroyed (Mayo-Kebi Ouest, Batha, Ennedi Ouest); 2020: ~20 provinces, ~388,000 people affected; 2021: 256,214 people affected (Tandjilé, Mandoul, Moyen-Chari, Logone Oriental most hit), 79,066 ha crops destroyed, 6,056 livestock lost; 2022: worst on record — 18/23 provinces, 1,468,847 people impacted, 465,030 ha crops flooded, 162,917 households affected, 78,949 homes destroyed, 19,399 livestock lost; N'Djamena alone ~192,337 people affected, 32,050 households.

--- page 9 ---
Chart (line chart): "Suivi des inondations de 2019-2024" — Personnes sinistrées (people affected) by year: 2019: 170,000; 2020: 380,000; 2021: 256,000; 2022: 1,468,847 (peak); 2023: 16,200 (low); 2024: 1,700,000 (as of 17 Sept 2024, highest value). Y-axis is number of people affected, X-axis is year.
Map pair: Two choropleth maps of Chad by department. Left map "Population totale typiquement exposée aux inondations" — color scale 0–200,000+ people; darkest/highest exposure concentrated in a small cluster in the south-west (around N'Djamena/Chari area). Right map "Fraction de la population typiquement exposée aux inondations" — color scale 0–0.20+; highest fraction (darkest purple) again clustered in south-west departments along the Chari river corridor, with a secondary highlighted patch further east/south. Based on FloodScan SFED flood extent (1998–2023) overlaid with WorldPop population data.

CDH + DRE/ANAM technicians: confirm 15-day mobilisation and/or 10-day action trigger reached, DRE/ANAM must confirm within 24 hours; communicated to CR, OCHA, CERF secretariat, GT AA via email/WhatsApp as thresholds are reached.

--- page 12 ---
Table (Protocole détaillé, continued): Secrétariat du CERF — sends approval letters to agencies immediately upon mobilisation/action trigger, interventions can start immediately. OCHA Tchad — informs ICC within 2 days, convenes GT AA meeting via email/WhatsApp. GT AA/agences participantes — inform local partners via WhatsApp/email. Coordonnateur Humanitaire (CH) — informs EHP and ministries at next HCT meeting or by email, ASAP after action trigger reached. OCHA Tchad (with CDH, DRE, ANAM) — continues monitoring flood evolution, sends impact maps by email to GT AA.
Narrative text: start of "Plan d'action anticipatoire" section — 4 selection criteria for actions: (1) Caractère anticipatoire, (2) Capacité à livrer dans la fenêtre d'opportunité, (3) Capacité opérationnelle, (4) Approche sans regret.

--- page 16 ---
Narrative text, no figure: Protection-VBG objective and UNFPA activity (cash transfers to GBV survivors via 4 one-stop centers in N'Djamena: hôpital mère-enfant, Tchad-chine, bon samaritain, notre dame des apôtres); partners AFJT, Maison Nationale de la Femme.
Table (Ciblage et préparation, targeting criteria by sector, part 1): Catégorie | Description (Responsable/Critères de ciblage/Méthodologie). ABNA: UNHCR, targets vulnerable people with destroyed shelters, via DTM + 2022 flood data. EAH: UNICEF, most-affected arrondissements via DTM+historical data, low sanitation access. Protection VBG: UNFPA, women/girls/boys with specific needs, via protection networks/projet 21/centres sociaux/community leaders. Santé: OMS/UNFPA, sinistrés needing care incl. pregnant women, under-5s, malnourished children, via community relay network.

--- page 17 ---
Table (Ciblage, continued): Sécurité Alimentaire — FAO: vulnerable households exposed to food insecurity, targeting via DRE forecasts/DTM 2024/key informants in high-risk neighborhoods, prioritizing stocks needing storage. PAM: communities in at-risk zones assessed by housing quality, resource access, economic status, vulnerable groups presence; validated with community leaders.
Narrative text: L'enregistrement des personnes ciblées (common beneficiary registration mechanism). Section 5 "Financements pré-convenues" begins — CERF: up to $5M pre-arranged for max 2 years, disbursed via CERF Rapid Response window; preconditions for disbursement listed (HC approval, ERC approval, trigger activation within 2 years).

--- page 18 ---
Narrative text: CERF disbursement process — two-stage mechanism (mobilisation trigger releases 100% of "mobilisation" portion; "action" portion released only if action trigger also reached before season end; unspent action funds refunded to CERF if action trigger not met). Administrative process for activation described.
Table (budget repartition, repeated): Secteur/Montant/Agences/Montant — same as page 1/3: ABNA $800,000(16%), EAH $850,000(17%), VBG $250,000(5%), Santé $800,000(16%), Sécurité alimentaire $2,300,000(46%); agencies UNHCR $600,000, OIM $350,000, UNICEF $700,000, UNFPA $550,000, OMS $500,000, FAO $800,000, PAM $1,500,000; Total $5,000,000.
Narrative text: Autres donateurs (framework aims for catalytic effect to mobilize additional bilateral funding). Section 6 "Apprentissage" begins — ad hoc learning/M&E committee convened by OCHA.

--- page 19 ---
Narrative text, no figure: Suivi et évaluation (S&E) — post-distribution monitoring (PDM), common M&E questions (impact on survival/quality of life, timing effectiveness, comparison vs past reactive response, multiplier effects). Evaluation indépendante — possible independent evaluation after activation, supported by sub-regional/regional/global teams.

--- page 20 ---
Table (Liste de points focaux principales): Partenaire | Nom | Rôle | Email — ~24 contacts across ANAM, DRE, FAO, OCHA, OIM, OMS, PAM, UNFPA, UNHCR, UNICEF (e.g., Djekounda Singambaye/ANAM/Director of Meteorological and Climatological Applications; Daouada Djouma/OCHA/Responsable coordination point focal AA; Milli Cooper/PAM/Anticipatory Action Officer; etc.).
Narrative text: Analyses du déclencheur — code on GitHub (OCHA-DAP/pa-aa-tcd-flooding); trigger backtested 2003-2022 against GloFAS reanalysis and historical ensemble forecasts; 4-year return period threshold (90% probability) corresponds to ~4,030 m³/s (2-year river level per GloFAS interface).

--- page 21 ---
Chart 1 (scatter plot): "Fleuve Chari à N'Djamena — Pics annuels GloFAS (2003-2022)". X-axis: Prévisions (% supérieur à période de retour 2 ans, délai 0-10 jours), 0-100%. Y-axis: Réanalyse (m³/s), 1000-7000. Horizontal red line "Seuil période de retour 4-ans" at ~4,600 m³/s. Vertical shaded band at 90-100% marks "Seuil période de retour 4-ans" trigger zone. Years at/near 100% forecast probability with high reanalysis (would have triggered): 2010 (~6,800), 2022 (~6,300), 2003 (~6,200), 2012 (~5,500), 2005 (~4,900) — all above the 4,600 threshold line, clustered at 90-100% on x-axis. Other years (2006,2007,2018,2020, etc.) cluster at lower forecast % (0-60%) and lower reanalysis values (1000-3700), not triggering. Text confirms: would have triggered in the five highest-discharge years (2010, 2022, 2003, 2012, 2005); 90% threshold chosen to correspond to 4-year return period.
Chart 2 (scatter plot): "Fleuve Chari à N'Djamena — Pics annuels GloFAS vs. observationnel (2003-2022)". X-axis: Niveau du fleuve observationnel (cm), 450-850. Y-axis: Réanalyse (m³/s), 1000-7000. Red horizontal line "Seuil période de retour 4-ans" (reanalysis, ~4,600 m³/s); green vertical line "Seuil période de retour 4-ans" (observational, ~700cm) dividing shaded red (upper-left, reanalysis-only trigger = false positives) vs green (lower-right, observational-only = false negatives) regions. Notable points: 2010 (~700cm,~6,800 - both triggered), 2022 (~820cm,~6,300), 2012 (~770cm,~5,500), 2003 (~695cm,~6,200 - reanalysis triggers but near observational line), 2005 (~630cm,~4,900 - false positive, reanalysis above threshold but observed below), 2020 (~700cm,~3,400) and 2019 (~690cm,~2,900) - false negatives (observed level high but reanalysis below threshold). Text confirms 2020 and 2019 would have had observed levels above the 4-year threshold but wouldn't have triggered (false negatives); 2003 and 2005 would have been false positives.

--- page 22 ---
Narrative text, no figure. States there is a significant temporal calibration gap between GloFAS reanalysis and observed river level: of 18 years analyzed, in 17 the reanalysis peak occurs earlier than the observed peak; average lag is 31 days.
